outcomes.text: The program identifies health administration, community health promotion, public health and large-scale data analysis as career preparation areas.

courses.name: First Year Seminar
courses.description: Supports university transition, community connections and student planning.

category_review.locator: CS 1200 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: University transition, resource use and personal planning fall outside the subject-matter categories; no programming content is established.

courses.name: College: An Introduction
courses.description: Introduces university life and health professions through community activities, academic skill development and connections with faculty and peers.

courses.name: First-Year Interdisciplinary Seminar
courses.description: Explores global citizenship, university resources and interdisciplinary problem solving.

category_review.locator: INPR 1000 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The first-year seminar emphasizes university resources and personal/academic development with global-challenge context, without a sufficiently specified substantive subject for this taxonomy.

courses.name: Professional Development for Khoury Co-op
courses.description: Prepares students for co-op applications, interviews and workplace expectations.

category_review.locator: CS 1210 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Co-op preparation, resumes, interviews and workplace conduct do not establish a primary computing subject category.

courses.name: Professional Development for Bouvé Co-op
courses.description: Prepares Bouvé students for co-op through career assessment, applications, interviews and review of workplace expectations and program procedures.

courses.name: Discrete Structures
courses.description: Develops discrete structures, logic, proofs and counting methods for computing.

category_review.locator: CS 1800 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Sets, relations, induction, proof, logic and counting form discrete mathematical methods; computing motivates their use.

courses.name: Introduction to Program Design and Implementation
courses.description: Introduces programming, dataset analysis and ethical issues in software design.

category_review.locator: CS 2000 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The course teaches program construction, coding and introductory data processing to students without programming experience.

courses.name: Lab for CS 2000
courses.description: Provides experiments supporting introductory programming coursework.

category_review.locator: CS 2001 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The lab explicitly accompanies the introductory program-design course and practices its computing topics.

courses.name: Program Design and Implementation 1
courses.description: Develops program design, object-oriented abstractions and software engineering practices.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 200M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: CS 2100 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Data/object-oriented design, data structures, abstraction, testing and software construction are the central methods.

courses.name: Lab for CS 2100
courses.description: Provides experiments supporting program design coursework.

category_review.locator: CS 2101 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The lab explicitly accompanies the reviewed program-design and software-construction course.

courses.name: Introduction to Databases
courses.description: Develops relational database design, SQL and introductory database-system techniques.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 200M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2500 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D- or EECE 2560 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: CS 3200 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Relational database design, query processing, indexing, concurrency and recovery are database-system methods.

courses.name: Advanced Programming with Data
courses.description: Develops robust software architectures and data pipelines using substantial datasets.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 3500 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Software architectures, reusable APIs, testing and maintainable data pipelines center on general software design and implementation.

courses.name: Principles of Human-Computer Interaction
courses.description: Introduces human-centered interface design, prototyping and usability evaluation.

category_review.locator: CS 2484 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Human-centered interface design, prototyping and usability evaluation constitute applied interaction-design practice, rather than general programming or an AI method.

courses.name: Mathematical Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Studies the mathematical basis of AI through linear algebra, probability and computational exercises.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2510 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 3000 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The description explicitly emphasizes linear algebra, probability and numerical mathematical foundations, using AI as their motivating application.

courses.name: Information Presentation and Visualization
courses.description: Studies how to design, implement and evaluate visual representations of data.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2510 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 4200 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Visualization combines programming, perception, visual communication and domain presentation; the description does not establish one defensible primary category among these.

courses.name: Large-Scale Information Storage and Retrieval
courses.description: Studies scalable data storage, distributed databases and retrieval methods.
courses.prerequisites: ( CS 3100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 310M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 3500 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 3500 with a minimum grade of D- ); CS 3200 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 4300 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Distributed databases, storage architectures, reliability and data retrieval are computing infrastructure methods.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.description: Introduces predictive modeling and major supervised and unsupervised learning methods.
courses.prerequisites: DS 3000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 250M with a minimum grade of D- or ( MATH 2331 with a minimum grade of D- ; MATH 3081 with a minimum grade of D- )

category_review.locator: DS 4400 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Supervised and unsupervised learning, predictive models, model evaluation and learning algorithms are the explicit central content.

courses.name: Calculus 1 for Science and Engineering
courses.description: Develops differentiation, its scientific applications, and introductory integration.

category_review.locator: MATH 1341 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Limits, differentiation, integration and the fundamental theorem of calculus are the central content.

courses.name: Calculus 1
courses.description: Introduces differentiation, integration and applications involving change and accumulation.

category_review.locator: MATH 1241 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The description teaches differentiation and integration, their techniques and mathematical applications.

courses.name: First-Year Writing
courses.description: Develops research and writing across audiences and genres through workshop practice.

category_review.locator: ENGW 1111 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The workshop teaches rhetorical choices, research-based writing, audience awareness and revision in academic, professional and public communication.

courses.name: First-Year Writing for Multilingual Writers
courses.description: Develops research, revision and writing practices with attention to multilingual writers.

category_review.locator: ENGW 1102 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The description teaches writing, rhetorical choices and communication across audiences and genres, with support for multilingual writers; it is not programming.

courses.name: Advanced Writing in the Technical Professions
courses.description: Develops research and communication in technical and professional genres.
courses.prerequisites: ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1113 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1114 with a minimum grade of C

category_review.locator: ENGW 3302 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Technical reports, proposals and presentations are the genres used to teach audience analysis, critical research and revision; the subject is technical communication rather than engineering methods.

courses.name: Interdisciplinary Advanced Writing in the Disciplines
courses.description: Develops research, revision and writing across disciplinary contexts.
courses.prerequisites: ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1113 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1114 with a minimum grade of C

category_review.locator: ENGW 3315 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Interdisciplinary professional, public and academic writing is taught through audience analysis, critical research, peer review and revision.

courses.name: The U.S. Healthcare System
courses.description: Examines healthcare organization, financing, access, equity and reform in the United States.

courses.name: Comparative Healthcare Systems
courses.description: Study-abroad comparison of healthcare access, financing, patient rights, technology and workforce issues in the United States and host country.

courses.name: Communication Skills for the Health Professions
courses.description: Develops interpersonal communication and presentation skills for health professions.

courses.name: Communication Skills for the Health Professions—Global
courses.description: Practices interpersonal, public and organizational health communication while comparing host-country and U.S. healthcare contexts.

courses.name: Community and Public Health
courses.description: Introduces population-health practice, the U.S. public health system, prevention and social inequalities in health.

courses.name: Community and Public Health - Global
courses.description: Compares U.S. and host-country public health systems through urban cases, disease burdens, social inequalities and environmental risks.

courses.name: Healthcare Policy and Administration
courses.description: Examines healthcare management, financing and policy through analysis and policy briefs.
courses.prerequisites: PHTH 1260 with a minimum grade of C or PHTH 1261 with a minimum grade of C or NYC 151M with a minimum grade of C

courses.name: Global Perspectives on Discrimination and Health
courses.description: Studies how discrimination and social categories shape health disparities using perspectives from anthropology, medicine and public health.
courses.prerequisites: ( COMM 3409 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3302 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3304 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3306 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3307 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3308 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3314 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3315 with a minimum grade of C ); ( PHTH 2350 with a minimum grade of C or PHTH 2351 with a minimum grade of C or PBH 110M with a minimum grade of C )

courses.name: Principles of Epidemiology in Medicine and Public Health
courses.description: Develops critical reading of epidemiological research through study design, bias, causal inference and methodological limitations; no computation is required.
courses.prerequisites: BIOE 2365 with a minimum grade of C or CRIM 3700 with a minimum grade of C or ECON 2350 with a minimum grade of C or BUSM 22EM with a minimum grade of C or ENVR 2500 with a minimum grade of C or INSH 3102 with a minimum grade of C or MATH 2280 with a minimum grade of C or MATH 3081 with a minimum grade of C or MGSC 2301 with a minimum grade of C or BUSM 224M with a minimum grade of C or NRSG 5120 with a minimum grade of C or PHTH 2210 with a minimum grade of C or POLS 2400 with a minimum grade of C or PSYC 2320 with a minimum grade of C or SOCL 2320 with a minimum grade of C

courses.name: Health Education and Program Planning
courses.description: Develops a health-program plan through needs assessment, intervention design, evaluation, budgeting and communication.
courses.prerequisites: COMM 3409 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3302 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3304 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3306 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3307 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3308 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3314 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3315 with a minimum grade of C

courses.name: Statistics for Economists
courses.description: Applies statistical inference, regression and data visualization to economic and social questions.
courses.prerequisites: (CS 1100 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2000 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 200M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2100 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2500 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2000 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MISM 2510 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- )

category_review.locator: ECON 2350 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Sampling, estimation, hypothesis tests and regression are statistical methods, with economics providing the data context.

courses.name: Biostatistics
courses.description: Develops probability, inference and experimental design for biological data analysis.

courses.name: Lab for ENVR 2500
courses.description: Applies biostatistical methods through supervised R laboratory exercises.

courses.name: Recitation for ENVR 2500
courses.description: Provides interactive practice applying biostatistics concepts.

courses.name: Probability and Statistics
courses.description: Develops probability distributions and limit theory, then introduces statistical inference.
courses.prerequisites: MATH 1342 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 211M with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1252 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1242 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: MATH 3081 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Probability distributions, expectation, limit theorems and statistical inference are the core content.

courses.name: Foundations of Biostatistics
courses.description: Applies biostatistical reasoning and R to clinical and public-health questions.

courses.name: Statistics in Psychological Research
courses.description: Develops statistical analysis and inference for psychological research.
courses.prerequisites: PSYC 1101 with a minimum grade of D- or (PSYC 101M with a minimum grade of D- ; PSYC 102M with a minimum grade of D- )

courses.name: Technology and Human Values
courses.description: Examines technology’s social dimensions and ethical implications.

courses.name: Moral and Social Problems in Healthcare
courses.description: Applies ethical frameworks to healthcare dilemmas involving consent, confidentiality, research, end-of-life decisions and resource allocation.

courses.name: General Biology 1
courses.description: Introduces cells, heredity, energy and biological inquiry through evolutionary perspectives.

category_review.locator: BIOL 1111 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Cell anatomy/physiology, reproduction, heredity and protein synthesis establish biological science; societal examples contextualize those biological concepts.

courses.name: Lab for BIOL 1111
courses.description: Develops biological experimentation, quantitative analysis and written reporting.
courses.prerequisites: BIOL 1111 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: BIOL 1112 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Experimental and simulation work accompanies BIOL 1111 biology; statistical analysis and writing are supporting lab practices.

courses.name: General Biology 2
courses.description: Examines organismal diversity, multicellular biology and ecological relationships.
courses.prerequisites: BIOL 1101 with a minimum grade of D- or BIOL 1107 with a minimum grade of D- or BIOL 1111 with a minimum grade of D- or BIOL 1115 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: BIOL 1113 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Organismal diversity, integrative biology and ecological relationships are substantive biological-science content.

courses.name: Lab for BIOL 1113
courses.description: Investigates general biology concepts through laboratory experiments.
courses.prerequisites: BIOL 1113 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: BIOL 1114 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Experiments accompany BIOL 1113 organismal and ecological biology.

courses.name: General Chemistry for Science Majors
courses.description: Introduces chemical structure, reactions, kinetics and thermodynamics with biological applications.

category_review.locator: CHEM 1161 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Chemical bonding, molecular interactions, kinetics and thermodynamics establish chemical-science content, with living systems as examples.

courses.name: Lab for CHEM 1161
courses.description: Develops laboratory techniques for studying chemical and physical processes.

category_review.locator: CHEM 1162 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The lab teaches chemical laboratory techniques, analysis and chemical/physical processes accompanying CHEM 1161.

courses.name: Recitation for CHEM 1161
courses.description: Provides guided practice applying concepts from general chemistry lectures.

category_review.locator: CHEM 1163 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The zero-hour recitation applies the chemical concepts of the accompanying CHEM 1161 lecture.

courses.name: Foundations of Psychology
courses.description: Surveys psychological research methods and major areas of behavioral science.

courses.name: Advanced Machine Learning
courses.description: Studies advanced learning methods and their mathematical and computational foundations.
courses.prerequisites: DS 4400 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 4420 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Advanced learning algorithms, structured-data models, Bayesian estimation and generative models are explicitly machine-learning content.

courses.name: Seminar for CS 1800
courses.description: Reinforces CS 1800 discrete-structures material through seminar discussion, quizzes and assignments.

category_review.locator: CS 1802 seminar description, together with CS 1800 discrete-structures description and reciprocal corequisite conditions
category_review.rationale: The seminar accompanies the explicitly reviewed discrete-structures course and reinforces its mathematical topics through discussion and assignments.
